issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares getTotalNumberOfStudents() with return type String, while the solution implementation defines getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return an int. The problem text even instructs students to check the UML for the expected return type, which would lead them to implement a String-returning method; however the reference implementation (and likely tests) use an int. This mismatch can cause students to implement the wrong return type and fail compilation or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent. Either update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (and clarify the text to expect an int), or change the solution implementation to return a String (e.g., return Integer.toString(numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents)) and adjust any dependent methods/tests accordingly. The preferred fix is to change the UML to int so numeric operations (like getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor()) remain natural and unambiguous.
